title: Mirror sign/scale orbit audit
hypothesis: On trained one-hidden-layer MLPs, ReLU positive rescaling (incoming weights/bias times s, outgoing rows divided by s) and tanh hidden sign flips (incoming weights/bias and outgoing rows sign-flipped) preserve test outputs within max difference 1e-5 after FP16 serialization. Such coordinate variants are zero additional function multiplicity.
physical_object: one trained 8-12-3 ReLU or tanh MLP
mirror_coordinate: per-hidden-unit positive scale for ReLU or sign code for tanh
logical_multiplicity: parameter coordinate variants in a function-preserving monomial symmetry orbit
controls: ReLU positive rescaling with reciprocal outgoing scale
tanh sign flip with coupled incoming/outgoing sign changes

development.selection_metric: max/RMS held-out output difference after FP16 reload

storage.authority: actual deterministic fixed-timestamp ZIP/NPY FP16 payload bytes

success_gate: FP32 function outputs under both symmetries differ by <=1e-5 in all three fresh seeds; FP16 quantization error is separately measured against each FP32 function; negative controls change outputs. Classify symmetry coordinates as zero new functions regardless of representation storage.
failure_gate: Correctly coupled FP32 transformations consistently change outputs beyond 1e-5, indicating a symmetry implementation failure and NOT ESTABLISHED status.
amendment: Development showed separate FP16 rounding of rescaled weights can create ~0.007 max output difference even when the FP32 reparameterization is invariant. Before fresh access, the audit separates algebraic FP32 symmetry difference from base/view FP16 quantization errors; seeds are unchanged and no model settings changed.
boundaries: exact symmetry audit, not a compression claim
tanh sign flips must couple incoming and outgoing tensors
coordinate orbit size is not functional capacity
